analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | KEYS | DE guide | AVAV takes
key_insights: Pre-market 11/20: S&P futures down 50bps as the technology sell-off continues. Asia fell hardest (Taiwan -623bps, KOSPI -521bps, Japan -506bps as written in the note) and Germany led Europe lower at -165bps.
German PPI printed 8.1% against 7.1% expected. French data was mixed, with a worse business survey but better manufacturing activity.

The note reports sharp CTA liquidation in commodities this week, with copper, gold and crude still for sale. The 10-year yield fell back below 5% to 4.98% on growth-scare fears, the dollar was flat and Bitcoin held at a lower level of $61.8k.
DE reports fiscal Q4 and guides fiscal 2027 next week. The stock has been 50/50 on the day over the last several years when DE guides.

Corporate commentary on ag has improved: DE said its early order program was up 5% at its last report and CNH and AGCO raised the bar at 15-20%. The note says this covers a small share of actual sales (planters, sprayers). North American ag, particularly large ag, shows the most green shoots, while Europe and Brazil remain downside risks.

The DE fundamental backdrop has deteriorated even as commentary improved. Crop prices have fully retreated after spiking this fall, the equity has sold off with the broader market, and multiples have expanded beyond historical norms while earnings are likely at trough.

GS investor conversations expect a DE net income guide near $5.7bn at the starting midpoint, below the $6.1bn consensus. GS leans negative on DE over the next six months but calls the print itself unclear because most investors expect the same thing.

DE trades at $625 against $700 earlier and is approaching $615 support at the 200-day average. GS says earnings very likely trough in fiscal 2026, but the 25%+ rebound embedded in consensus looks realistic at best and aggressive at worst.
KEYS Q4 EPS was $3.61 against $3.37 consensus on revenue of $1.99bn against $1.95bn consensus. Orders were $8.13bn (+49% y/y, book to bill above 1x) and gross margin was 69.3% (+460bps y/y).
KEYS guided Q1 EPS to $3.63-3.69 against $3.21 and revenue to $2.04-2.06bn against $1.96bn consensus. The options market implied a 10% move into the print.

GS relays an investor view it agrees with: the market wants to see misses and cuts to form a bottom so AI-related stocks can start reacting, so beating, raising and guiding ahead is currently more problematic.
CW expanded its share repurchase program by $250mm, bringing planned 2026 repurchases to $710mm.

AVAV (GIR dinner takeaways): after F1Q it had visibility into 86% of full-year revenue guidance. It has since announced a ~$315mn award under a $940mn IDIQ contract (converting to revenue in 12-18 months) and a $405mn Middle East order for LOCUST X3 (12-24 months), which implies the year is close to 100% sold. F2Q book-to-bill should be strong.

AVAV budget view: management sees a strong funding environment and is not particularly concerned about a short continuing resolution given backlog. It does not expect additional large reconciliation dollars in the final FY2027 budget but expects the FY27 base to be higher than FY26. Unmanned, counter-drone and space remain high Pentagon priorities with substantial international demand.

AVAV margins: the 2026 Investor Day target is EBITDA margin expansion from 14.5% (FY26) to 18-20% (FY30), helped by higher international and fixed-price mix and in-sourcing of manufacturing components.
GS hosts a WWD earnings callback with investor relations at 10am on Zoom on 11/20. Upcoming GS events run through 12/10, including the GS Industrials and Materials Conference on 12/2-12/3.

tension_points.bull_case: Corporate commentary is building positively: DE's early order program was up 5% and CNH and AGCO raised the bar at 15-20%. North American large ag shows green shoots and earnings are very likely to trough in fiscal 2026.
tension_points.bear_case: Crop prices have fully retreated, the equity has sold off with the market and multiples have expanded beyond historical norms. Investors expect a net income guide near $5.7bn against $6.1bn consensus, so the 25%+ rebound in consensus looks aggressive.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A fiscal 2027 net income guide midpoint near $5.7bn rather than the $6.1bn consensus, or a break of $615 support at the 200-day average.
